nodes.title: Build Brunch as a local spec-elicitation product layered on Pi without forking it
Surface cross-session graph changes to the agent coherently at turn boundaries
Offer-first structured exchange elicits better spec truth than free-form chat
Pi's linear JSONL transcript can be the single canonical session substrate
Spec

detail.definition: A user-created elicitation subject: one graph of intent/oracle/design/plan truth with its own spec-local LSN clock.

nodes.title: Session exchange

detail.definition: The unit spanning one structured offer-and-response (or a plain user message) projected from the linear transcript.

nodes.title: Lens

detail.definition: The topical-focus axis of the session agent (intent / design / oracle).

nodes.title: Strategy

detail.definition: The reusable interaction-shape axis of the session agent.

nodes.title: Readiness grade

detail.definition: A forward gate over a spec, advancing grounding to elicitation to commitment to planning.

nodes.title: Pi supplies the TUI harness, JSONL sessions, and extension hooks Brunch builds on
Stakeholders want the TUI and web to share one data plane, not two
A minority view wants Brunch to fork Pi for deeper control
All durable graph mutations route through one CommandExecutor authority
A public RPC agent-as-user can drive structured exchanges without speaking raw Pi RPC
Graph context reads support a compact overview and a node-neighborhood detail view
Spec/session selection is a reusable hierarchical decision model
Every session turn must follow the offer-first present/request ritual
Offer-first applies per strategy, not as a universal per-turn session invariant
Pi linear JSONL sessions suffice as transcript truth for the POC
Local POC graph and session sizes stay small enough to defer performance budgets
Brunch must not fork Pi
A Brunch-launched Pi runtime must not load ambient user/project .pi resources
The browser must not require a second primary data plane
One spec-local LSN per commit; exactly one graph_clock row per spec
mutateGraph batch validation is all-or-nothing
Same-spec supersession edges form an acyclic directed graph
Node kind is a per-plane closed enum validated by the CommandExecutor
Adopt a single CommandExecutor mutation authority

detail.chosen_option: Route every durable mutation through one CommandExecutor command boundary
rejected: Let callers write the graph store directly
detail.rationale: One authority centralizes validation, audit, LSN allocation, and coherence triggering.

nodes.title: Split the session agent into orthogonal Strategy and Lens axes

detail.chosen_option: Two orthogonal axes: Strategy (interaction shape) and Lens (topical focus)
rejected: A single flat free-text elicitation-lens catalogue
detail.rationale: Orthogonal axes compose cleanly and keep routing legible.

nodes.title: Compose prompts as a thin runtime header plus a gated resource manifest

detail.chosen_option: Thin runtime header + gated <available_*> manifest; bodies loaded on demand by read
rejected: Eager concatenation of every objective pack
detail.rationale: Projection over a state machine keeps prompts small and legal per turn.

nodes.title: Add freestyle as a structure-optional strategy that AUTO must never select

detail.chosen_option: freestyle is an explicit user pin only; AUTO omits it
rejected: Make freestyle a new operational mode
detail.rationale: Spontaneous AUTO entry would silently abandon the offer-first product thesis.
